Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "please revise this handoff note so it reads clearly, but keep it as a practical note for the payroll team. we are preparing the payroll export for the april 1 through april 15, 2025 pay period, and the export is scheduled to be reviewed on may 2. the file goes to the payroll operations folder after review, not to the shared finance folder, because that folder has a wider audience. the export covers 184 employees across 6 departments and 3 pay groups. those numbers describe the population in this run, the department count, and the pay group count, respectively; they are not targets for a later run.

please keep the export name exactly as shown here, on its own line, because the upload checklist compares the name character by character:
speaker-rota.csv

this file is built from the timekeeping extract and the current employee roster. the timekeeping extract was pulled at 9:15 am on may 1, and the roster was refreshed at 11:40 am on may 1. those are the source times, not the time the export is created. if either source is refreshed after those times, the payroll analyst needs to rebuild the export before review, rather than just changing the date in the note. the timekeeping team said, “we corrected the missed clock-out entries for the west clinic before the extract was pulled.” please keep that as a report from the team, not a separate claim from the writer.

for the export, the gross pay column is in dollars and cents, the hours column is in decimal hours, and the department field uses the short department codes from the roster. the report contains 12 columns, and the last column is the exception note. there are 7 rows with an exception note in this run; that count is the number of employee rows needing a look, not the number of separate issues. the payroll analyst should compare those rows with the signed timecards and add a comment in the review log if a correction is needed. no one should change an employee’s base rate from this export alone.

1. before review, check the row count against the 184 employees in the roster and confirm that all 6 department codes appear. also check that the 3 pay groups are labeled hourly, salaried, and seasonal, in that order in the export. the sequence matters because the payroll operations import reads the groups from top to bottom. if a department has no employee rows in this pay period, do not add a blank row just to make its code appear; report the missing code to the analyst instead.

2. review the 7 exception-note rows against signed timecards, and compare any revised hours with the timekeeping extract. if a timecard is still waiting for a supervisor signature on may 2, leave that row flagged and ask the supervisor for the signed copy; do not treat an unsigned card as confirmation. the payroll lead said, “we can hold those rows while the rest of the file is checked.” that is the lead’s option for handling the review, not confirmation that any rows have already been held.

3. save the reviewed export in the payroll operations folder and enter the source refresh times, the review date, and any corrections in the review log. use the date format YYYY-MM-DD in the log, even though the export itself displays dates as MM/DD/YYYY. the finance team requested a copy for its monthly reconciliation, but send that copy only after the payroll analyst confirms that the review is complete. until then, keep the file in the payroll operations folder and do not send it to the shared finance folder.

please also note that the schedule is tight because the payroll operations import is planned for 5:00 pm on may 2, while the review is scheduled for 4:30 pm that day. those times are the planned import and review times, not proof that either event has happened. if the analyst finds a mismatch between the roster count and the export, the analyst should pause the review and contact payroll operations before the planned import. if the counts match but an exception remains unresolved, leave the exception visible in the review log and use the lead’s hold option for that row; do not silently remove it from the file.

the handoff should make clear that the payroll analyst is responsible for checking the source timestamps, row count, department codes, pay-group order, and exception notes. payroll operations is responsible for receiving the file in its folder and completing the import after the review. the finance copy is a separate later step, and it depends on the analyst confirming completion. the note should not imply that the export is already approved, that the import is complete, or that a correction has been made when those things are still pending. please keep the details about the west clinic clock-out correction attributed to the timekeeping team, and keep the lead’s statement about holding rows as an option rather than a completed action.

for the final review record, include which of the 7 exception rows were checked, whether a signed timecard was available for each one, and any correction entered in the review log. if a correction is not needed, record that the row was checked without changing its hours. if a signed card is unavailable, record that status and leave the row flagged for follow-up. keep the source refresh times and the review date in the log even if the export is rebuilt, so the team can tell which inputs were used for the file under review. the May 2 schedule should remain described as planned unless the team updates the record after the events occur. The finance copy should remain pending unless the analyst confirms the review is complete.", "output": "Please revise this handoff note so it reads clearly while remaining practical for the payroll team. We are preparing the payroll export for the April 1 through April 15, 2025 pay period, and the export is scheduled for review on May 2. After review, the file goes to the payroll operations folder, not the shared finance folder, which has a wider audience. This run covers 184 employees across 6 departments and 3 pay groups. Those figures describe the employee population, department count, and pay group count for this run; they are not targets for a later run.

Please keep the export name exactly as shown here, on its own line, because the upload checklist compares the name character by character:

The file is built from the timekeeping extract and the current employee roster. The extract was pulled at 9:15 am on May 1, and the roster was refreshed at 11:40 am on May 1. These are the source times, not the export creation time. If either source is refreshed after those times, the payroll analyst needs to rebuild the export before review rather than simply changing the date in the note. The timekeeping team said, “we corrected the missed clock-out entries for the west clinic before the extract was pulled.” Keep this attributed to the team rather than presenting it as a separate claim by the writer.

In the export, the gross pay column is in dollars and cents, the hours column is in decimal hours, and the department field uses the short department codes from the roster. The report contains 12 columns, with the exception note in the last column. This run has 7 rows with an exception note. That is the number of employee rows needing review, not the number of separate issues. The payroll analyst should compare those rows with the signed timecards and add a comment to the review log if a correction is needed. No one should change an employee’s base rate based on this export alone.

1. Before review, check the row count against the 184 employees in the roster and confirm that all 6 department codes appear. Also check that the 3 pay groups are labeled hourly, salaried, and seasonal, in that order in the export. The sequence matters because the payroll operations import reads the groups from top to bottom. If a department has no employee rows in this pay period, do not add a blank row just to display its code; report the missing code to the analyst instead.

2. Review the 7 rows with exception notes against signed timecards, and compare any revised hours with the timekeeping extract. If a timecard is still awaiting a supervisor’s signature on May 2, leave that row flagged and ask the supervisor for the signed copy. Do not treat an unsigned card as confirmation. The payroll lead said, “we can hold those rows while the rest of the file is checked.” This is the lead’s option for handling the review, not confirmation that any rows have already been held.

3. Save the reviewed export in the payroll operations folder and enter the source refresh times, review date, and any corrections in the review log. Use the YYYY-MM-DD date format in the log, even though the export itself displays dates as MM/DD/YYYY. The finance team requested a copy for its monthly reconciliation, but send it only after the payroll analyst confirms that the review is complete. Until then, keep the file in the payroll operations folder and do not send it to the shared finance folder.

The schedule is tight: the payroll operations import is planned for 5:00 pm on May 2, while the review is scheduled for 4:30 pm that day. These are the planned import and review times, not proof that either event has happened. If the analyst finds a mismatch between the roster count and the export, the analyst should pause the review and contact payroll operations before the planned import. If the counts match but an exception remains unresolved, leave it visible in the review log and use the lead’s hold option for that row; do not silently remove it from the file.

The handoff should make clear that the payroll analyst is responsible for checking the source timestamps, row count, department codes, pay-group order, and exception notes. Payroll operations is responsible for receiving the file in its folder and completing the import after review. The finance copy is a separate later step, dependent on the analyst confirming that the review is complete. The note should not imply that the export is already approved, that the import is complete, or that a correction has been made while those items are still pending. Keep the details about the west clinic clock-out correction attributed to the timekeeping team, and present the lead’s statement about holding rows as an option rather than a completed action.

For the final review record, include which of the 7 exception rows were checked, whether a signed timecard was available for each one, and any correction entered in the review log. If no correction is needed, record that the row was checked without changing its hours. If a signed card is unavailable, record that status and leave the row flagged for follow-up. Keep the source refresh times and review date in the log even if the export is rebuilt, so the team can identify which inputs were used for the file under review. Describe the May 2 schedule as planned unless the team updates the record after the events occur. The finance copy should remain pending unless the analyst confirms that the review is complete."}]
